scope_outcomes.criterion: A condition qualifies when varying, granting, or assuming it performs an identifiable inferential task, including counterfactuals, open conditionals, and even-if concessions.
scope_outcomes.basis: The article contains an explicit even-if concession, an explicit counterfactual identity test, and an open conditional concerning capitalism.
limitations: Classification concerns argumentative suppositions in the supplied article, not the validity of all cited sources.
No distinct reductio was retained: rhetorical questions support the identity argument but do not clearly assume a rejected proposition to derive a contradiction.

scope_outcomes.criterion: Retain conditions explicitly varied or held fixed and identify reconstructed constraints or additional premises needed for the consequent.
scope_outcomes.basis: The text varies recognition monism while holding fixed the demand for a comprehensive critical theory, and characterizes the comprehensive moral grammar as Honneth’s defining contribution.
limitations: The scenarios are conceptual rather than historical, so no earlier historical backtracking conditions were required.
Some held-fixed standards are reconstructed from adjacent statements rather than expressed with all-else-equal wording.

scope_outcomes.criterion: The antecedent-to-consequent bridge must be inspectable as a conceptual, definitional, causal, historical, or normative warrant with its modal scope preserved.
scope_outcomes.basis: The text supplies a definitional bridge from monism to theoretical identity and causal-conceptual bridges from impersonal or structural forces to recognition theory’s explanatory limits.
limitations: The universal claim about every social pathology is asserted more broadly than the detailed examples demonstrate.
The comparative standard implied by the word “optimally” is not independently specified.

scope_outcomes.criterion: A relevant alternative must be available in the text and compare the same explanatory task while identifying changes in framework, role, modality, or scope.
scope_outcomes.basis: The article presents Fraser’s pluralist alternative, which retains recognition for some struggles while assigning other pathologies to other approaches.
limitations: The article does not fully develop or empirically test a pluralist successor that gives recognition only a subordinate role.
The Thompson alternative concerns replacement foundations and is not itself a controlled test of recognition’s limited usefulness.

scope_outcomes.criterion: Withdraw one premise or route at a time and distinguish loss of a formulation from loss of the conclusion where independent support remains.
scope_outcomes.basis: The article explicitly bases its final recommendation on the plurality and combined force of eight criticisms, allowing the identity argument and substantive inadequacy arguments to be separated.
limitations: The text does not individually perform every premise-withdrawal test; part of the robustness assessment is an analyst reconstruction.
The material establishes multiple independent critical routes but does not prove that every possible revised theory is defeated.
